title: Proactive capacity preflight checks and soft-eviction playbook for hosted GPU exhaustion
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: After the hosted API GPU exhaustion incident on 2026-02-14 we observed prolonged queue buildup for high-throughput tenants that prevented autoscaler priming and caused broad request throttling. This ticket defines a proactive 'preflight' capacity check, a predictive prewarm heuristic, and a soft-eviction/fallback playbook to reduce tail latency and avoid full pool exhaustion. The scope covers controller-side admission logic, prewarm orchestration, eviction scoring, and a phased rollout with monitoring and safety gates.
root_cause_summary: The immediate cause was a correlated surge from multiple high-concurrency tenants combined with a delayed autoscale trigger. Contributing factors: lack of a short-term forecast in admission controller, admission scoring that didn't penalize large long-lived KV cache sessions, and reactive autoscaler cooldown/hysteresis that slowed priming. Result: queue amplification, time-to-first-token regressions, and prioritized throttles that cascaded into tenant-level retries.
decisions: 1) Implement a 2-hour rolling short-term demand forecast in the admission controller instead of relying only on instantaneous queue length. 2) Introduce a predictive prewarm that reserves a small number of GPU slots when forecast exceeds threshold for a pool. 3) Soft-eviction policy: idle-first soft eject + fair-score that factors recent SLO violations and tenant priority. 4) Add a CPU-fallback mode for best-effort tenants to avoid blocking higher-priority traffic. 5) Deploy feature behind runtime-1.23 toggle and gated by metric thresholds.
action_items: A1: Implement rolling forecast service (2h window, 5m granularity) and expose API to admission controller — owner: Marcus; estimate: 3
A2: Add preflight check to admission controller to request prewarm N GPUs when forecast > X% of available capacity — owner: Elena Ruiz; estimate: 2
A3: Design soft-eviction scoring algorithm: score = alpha*idle_time + beta*recent_tokens + gamma*SLO_penalty + delta*tenant_priority — owner: Priya Shah; estimate: 3
A4: Implement CPU-fallback path for low-priority tenants with degraded-KV semantics and response headers indicating best-effort — owner: Marcus; estimate: 2
A5: Add dashboard & alerts: forecast breach, prewarm failures, soft-eviction rate, CPU-fallback utilization — owner: Observability team; estimate: 2
A6: Create canary rollout plan with 5% traffic on runtime-1.23 -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with kill-switch — owner: SRE; estimate: 1
A7: Write automated chaos test simulating correlated tenant surges to validate prewarm + soft-evict behavior — owner: Test infra; estimate: 3
A8: Document runbook updates and add step for fast rollback of prewarm (scale down) and eviction reversal — owner: Ops; estimate: 1
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Under synthetic correlated surge (modeled off 2026-02-14 traffic), median time-to-first-token improves by >=35% compared to baseline
AC2: Number of full-pool exhaustion events in 30-day synthetic tests is zero
AC3: Prewarm orchestration completes within target lead-time 60s for 90% of requests
AC4: Soft-eviction reduces forced eviction error rate by >=50% while preserving P95 latency for P0 tenants
AC5: CPU-fallback returns 200 with X-Redwood-Fallback header and keeps critical tenants unblocked
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Merge feature-flagged code to runtime-1.23 branch, e2e tests pass in CI
Phase 1: Internal canary with engineering-only traffic (5% of production) for 48 hours; monitor eviction counts and prewarm success
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 25% over 24 hours if metrics stable, run chaos test overnight
Phase 3: 50% for 72 hours with extended dashboards; pre-announce to on-call and SEs
Phase 4: Full rollout and remove feature gate after 7 days of stable metrics
open_questions: Q1: What forecast threshold (X%) balances prewarm cost vs avoided tail latency? (finance input required)
Q2: How to tune alpha/beta/gamma/delta weights in eviction score for fair tenant behavior? Propose A/B experiments.
Q3: Should CPU-fallback be opt-in per-tenant or controlled by org-level policy?
Q4: Does prewarm reserve permanent slots (risk of underutilization) or temporary burst slots?
